summary_plain: This ground-based investigation analyzed soot formation, flame structure, and radiation using data from the Smoke Point in Coflow Experiment. Researchers combined computational models with experimental images to understand how flames behave differently in microgravity compared to normal gravity. This work helps improve spacecraft fire safety and leads to cleaner combustion technologies.
summary_expert: The investigation integrated computational and experimental methods to derive temperature distributions and soot volume fractions from Smoke Point in Coflow Experiment data. Researchers analyzed over 1600 raw digital single-lens reflex images using color-ratio pyrometry and absolute light calibration to extract soot temperature fields and soot volume fractions. Coupled flow-species-soot simulations were performed for Yale and ACME burner configurations under normal and microgravity conditions, incorporating radiation re-absorption and discrete-sectional aggregate formation. The documents provided describe the objectives and design only.

key_findings.text: Microgravity conditions were hypothesized to produce longer, more diffuse flames with lower temperatures and increased soot concentrations compared to normal gravity.
The investigation analyzed over 1600 raw DSLR images and incorporated advanced soot models to understand soot formation, oxidation, radiative re-absorption, and aggregate growth.

Raw Nikon NEF images were decoded into three color channels and analyzed using color-ratio pyrometry to extract soot temperature fields, with absolute light calibration used to calculate soot volume fractions.

earth_applications: inform the design of cleaner energy and industrial systems
